subject: Region blip — failover instructions and PMO request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 16:15:00 +0000
Subject: Region blip — failover instructions and PMO request

Sanjay / Acme ops team —

Tl;dr: We observed a short-lived service degradation affecting the US edge cluster and intermittent POST token timeouts for a subset of requests originating from us-west. We recommended an immediate client-side failover to our eu-west endpoint while we stabilize. Below are practical steps and what we (Redwood) are doing next.

What happened (brief):
- 15:05 UTC: increased connection queueing at the us-west edge (network MUX layer).
- 15:12 UTC: partial request timeouts for long-context generations for ~2% of traffic.
- We mitigated by shifting new sessions to alternative regional ingress and flushing impacted routing caches.

Immediate actions for ACME (customer-facing steps):
1) Temporary endpoint swap (recommended): switch client endpoint to https://api.redwood.ai?region=eu-west until we confirm full stabilization. This preserves low-latency for EU-hosted traffic and bypasses the us-west ingress.
2) If you use region-prefixed hostnames: update the host to eu-west.api.redwood.ai for new sessions for the next 120 minutes.
3) Reduce max sequence length to 1024 for in-flight requests where possible (helps avoid long-tail inference timeouts).
4) If you have Dedicated capacity with us: ask your infra team to toggle the routing policy in Console -> Routes -> Fallbacks -> Force route to eu-west.

Why this helps: the degradation is concentrated at the us-west edge routing layer (not model backends). Routing to eu-west uses a different MUX cluster and will avoid the transient queuing.

What Redwood is doing:
- We have a mitigation runbook in progress (see attached mitigation-checklist.pdf).
- Eng is performing a deeper network sampling and will post a short postmortem; I’ll share the root cause summary and any required customer action items.
- We’ve opened INC-2029 and will update the public status page.

Attachments: traffic-routing-diagram.png (shows failover path), mitigation-checklist.pdf

Ask: please reply to confirm when you’ve pointed a small test client at eu-west and share a sample request-id (header x-redwood-request-id) if you see anything odd. If preferred, we can schedule a quick ops handoff call now.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Region blip — failover instructions and PMO request

Thanks Ben — quick update from our side.

- We pointed a staging client at eu-west.api.redwood.ai at 16:22 UTC and completed several 512-token generation runs. Latency looks normal; no timeouts observed so far.
- I’ll have our prod infra toggle the DNS-based fallback for 30 minutes to validate.

We saw one request with x-redwood-request-id: rwd-78a2f1b3 that returned a 504 at 15:17 UTC before we rerouted — attaching the logs here (excerpt).

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Region blip — operational next steps (internal)

Ben / Markus — forwarding the customer reply. Quick internal notes:

- Ask Eng to capture MUX metrics from 15:00–15:30 UTC and include TCP SYN/FIN rates from the us-west edge. We need queue depth histograms and the routing cache eviction timeline.
- Ops: prepare a brief customer-facing RCA template; we’ll need a timeline and impact bucket (e.g., 2% of requests, 15 min window).
- PMO: schedule a 30m sync with Acme for 10:30 UTC tomorrow to walk through remediation and any longer-term guidance (network peering changes, TTL adjustments).

I’ll take the PMO lead and draft the post-incident note. Markus, can you validate the mitigation-checklist.pdf and confirm we captured the right console steps for Dedicated customers?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability

Subject: Re: Region blip — failover instructions and PMO request

Sanjay — thanks for the quick confirmation and for the request-id. Follow-up and next steps: 

1) Status: our on-call confirmed the us-west MUX queue pressure cleared at 15:31 UTC after a configuration rollback and cache warmup. Public status updated (https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2029-region-blip).
2) Postmortem plan: Laura will own the PMO write-up; we’ll include timeline, root cause hypothesis, affected customer list, and recommended mitigations (including client-side region failover best practices). Expect a draft by EOD Monday (2029-06-17).
3) Action for ACME: please attach the full request headers for rwd-78a2f1b3 and any correlated logs around 15:10–15:25 UTC. That will speed the RCA.
4) Optional longer-term step: if you want sub-100ms tail latency from us for steady-state traffic, we can propose a Dedicated pool in eu-west and a regional peering arrangement; I can share an outline and cost estimate.

Proposed quick sync: Laura will send a calendar invite for 10:30 UTC tomorrow to do a short runbook walkthrough and confirm log handoff. If that time doesn't work, tell us a 60-min window and we’ll adjust.

Attachments (for reference): traffic-routing-diagram.png, mitigation-checklist.pdf

Thanks — we’ll keep monitoring and I’ll send the postmortem draft when ready.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
